Asset universe: No traded assets
Data and features used: Copernicus ECMWF 51, DWD 22 and CMCC 4 seasonal SST ensembles and hindcasts; ERA5; NOAA ERSSTv6 ONI; NOAA monthly Niño indices
Model or trading rule: Convert ensemble SST to Niño 3.4 seasonal anomalies and calibrate to ONI with ridge regression
Important parameters: CMCC selected on tuning data; ridge alpha 0.1; independent holdout; forecast uncertainty from ensemble/calibration draws
Main result: Forecast medians were +2.6, +3.0, +3.3 and +3.5 C for ASO through NDJ; CMCC holdout RMSE 0.294 C versus ECMWF 0.273 C and persistence 0.566 C
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained only as a scenario input. Forecasts exceeded training maxima and the tuning-selected model was not the ex-post best holdout model.

Asset universe: US states; no traded assets
Historical period: Historical NOAA state and climate-division records through 2026; target Sep-Dec 2026
Data and features used: NOAA NCEI state and climate-division temperature; calibrated ONI forecast; calendar-month indicators
Model or trading rule: State-by-calendar-month temperature regression on ONI with forecast draws propagated to state estimates
Important parameters: Report states only when central ENSO contribution exceeded +2 C; preserve residual weather uncertainty
Main result: Eleven states exceeded +2 C in December; North Dakota +4.0 C and Minnesota +3.9 C were largest. September and October added state skill was not demonstrated.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained for physical scenario analysis. It estimates an ENSO-associated contribution rather than total realized temperature or causal attribution.

Experiment name or identifier: EXP-02 Insurer return and volatility correlation
Asset universe: RNR, EG, ACGL; SPY benchmark
Data and features used: NOAA weekly Niño 3.4 and seasonal ONI; adjusted insurer and SPY prices; next-month return and realized volatility; calendar controls
Model or trading rule: Pearson, Spearman and partial correlations using only delayed ENSO observations
Important parameters: Weekly Niño delay 14 days with 28-day sensitivity; ONI eligible after season end plus 15 days; no interpolation; year-block bootstrap
Main result: Equal-weight insurance-basket ENSO versus next-month return r=-0.013. Volatility relations weakened materially in the 2017-2026 subperiod.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected as a stand-alone signal because effect size was near zero, signs were unstable and insurer earnings depend on many non-ENSO variables.

Asset universe: RNR, EG, ACGL equal-weight basket
Data and features used: Delayed warm, neutral and cold ENSO states; next-calendar-month negative-return indicator
Model or trading rule: Conditional decline probabilities and probability-calibration comparison with the unconditional decline rate
Important parameters: Warm at least +0.5 C; cold at most -0.5 C; probability accuracy measured by Brier score and Brier skill
Main result: Insurance-basket Brier skill was about -0.035. Warm, cold and neutral decline-rate intervals overlapped.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the model forecast probabilities worse than the unconditional baseline and did not separate ENSO states reliably.

Asset universe: RNR, EG, ACGL equal-weight basket; same-exposure comparator
Data and features used: Delayed ENSO state; monthly insurer-basket returns; transaction-cost assumptions; average exposure
Model or trading rule: Reduce insurer exposure under adverse fitted ENSO conditions and compare with always invested and a non-timing strategy with the same mean exposure
Important parameters: Expanding information set; mean exposure 94.8%; monthly rebalancing; costs charged
Main result: Overlay CAGR 10.37% versus 11.49% always invested and 10.99% for the same-exposure comparator; max drawdown remained about -35.5%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because lower exposure explained most of the result and the timing rule did not improve on the exposure-matched control.

Asset universe: ZC, ZS, ZW, ZM, ZL, ZO, ZR, KE, LE, GF, HE, CC, KC, CT, SB and OJ public futures quote histories
Historical period: Sep 2006-Sep 2026; about 238-239 complete months by series
Data and features used: NOAA weekly Niño 3.4 and ONI; public Yahoo futures quote histories; monthly log return and realized volatility
Model or trading rule: Delayed Pearson, Spearman and controlled correlation screen
Important parameters: At least 15 daily observations per month; first observation by day 7; last on or after day 25; reject returns across gaps over 7 calendar days
Main result: Broad agriculture quote basket ENSO versus next-month return was about r=-0.133; individual commodity signs and ENSO definitions varied.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected for direct trading because the quote paths did not preserve verified contract identities, expiration rolls or executable roll transactions.

Asset universe: DBA, CORN, SOYB and WEAT
Data and features used: Delayed ENSO signals; adjusted futures-based fund returns; fund methodology and embedded roll effects
Model or trading rule: Monthly defensive exposure overlay with transaction costs and always-invested comparison
Important parameters: No futures return splicing; funds used as investable proxies; costs charged
Main result: DBA overlay CAGR 3.91% versus 5.68% always invested.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because timing reduced return and the fund returns combine commodity exposure, roll rules, collateral and fees.

Asset universe: Copper, aluminum and nickel benchmark prices
Data and features used: User-supplied aligned monthly NOAA ONI and metal benchmark prices; ONI level; delta ONI; monthly metal log returns
Model or trading rule: Pearson correlation sweep across candidate leads and lags
Important parameters: Lags from -24 to +24 months; level and delta-ONI variants; raw p-values treated as descriptive
Main result: Best highlighted relations were delta-ONI lag 2 to copper r=-0.176, delta-ONI lag 2 to aluminum r=-0.153 and delta-ONI lag 8 to nickel r=+0.100.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Modified into a walk-forward experiment because the full-sample lag search had selection bias and did not represent a frozen tradable rule.

Asset universe: Copper benchmark
Data and features used: Delayed ONI and delta ONI; copper monthly log returns; lag candidates estimated only on training data
Model or trading rule: Expanding training sample; select signal and lag; freeze for the next 12-month test block
Important parameters: Two-month ONI delay plus one-month gap; 25 frozen blocks; transaction costs; HAC mean test and OOS information coefficient
Main result: Annualized return 8.32%; Sharpe 0.48; max drawdown -49.63%; HAC p=0.073; IC=0.089 with p=0.129.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as a weak research lead only. It was closest to significance but had large drawdown and no 5% evidence in mean return or IC.

Asset universe: Aluminum benchmark
Data and features used: Delayed ONI and delta ONI; aluminum monthly log returns
Model or trading rule: Expanding training sample with frozen 12-month test blocks
Important parameters: Two-month ONI delay plus one-month gap; 25 blocks; modal rule delta-ONI lag 3
Main result: Annualized return 1.24%; Sharpe 0.16; max drawdown -74.36%; HAC p=0.519; IC=-0.036 with p=0.537.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because return, IC and drawdown did not support a tradable effect.

Asset universe: Nickel benchmark
Data and features used: Delayed ONI and delta ONI; nickel monthly log returns
Model or trading rule: Expanding training sample with frozen 12-month test blocks
Important parameters: Two-month ONI delay plus one-month gap; 25 blocks; selected lag allowed to update from past data
Main result: Annualized return -14.81%; Sharpe -0.41; max drawdown -98.70%; HAC p=0.096; IC=-0.164 with p=0.005.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the signal forecast the wrong economic sign for the implemented rule and produced a near-total drawdown.

Asset universe: MOD, VRT, JCI, ETN, TT, CARR and related infrastructure names versus copper, aluminum and nickel
Data and features used: Monthly metal returns; monthly cooling-infrastructure equity returns; candidate lags
Model or trading rule: Pearson correlation across metals and lagged monthly stock targets
Important parameters: Candidate lags selected descriptively; no trade costs at this stage
Main result: Nickel return lag 3 to VRT was strongest highlighted relation: r=-0.343, raw p=0.0022, n=77.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Modified into walk-forward tests because raw correlation was selected from many metal, lag and stock combinations.

Asset universe: VRT versus copper, aluminum and nickel
Data and features used: Lagged metal returns; VRT monthly return; expanding training data
Model or trading rule: Choose the strongest prior metal/lag specification and freeze it for the next test block
Important parameters: Two frozen blocks; modal rule nickel return lag 3; costs charged
Main result: Annualized return 42.35%; Sharpe 0.87; max drawdown -25.32%; HAC p=0.0815; OOS IC=-0.029 with p=0.911.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected as validated alpha because only 17 months were tested and the signal-return IC was essentially zero despite high realized PnL.

Asset universe: VRT
Data and features used: Delayed ONI and delta ONI; VRT monthly return
Model or trading rule: Expanding training and frozen test blocks
Important parameters: Two frozen blocks; modal rule delta-ONI lag 0
Main result: Annualized return 25.44%; Sharpe 0.68; max drawdown -34.42%; HAC p=0.282; IC=-0.170 with p=0.514.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the sample had two blocks and neither mean-return nor IC evidence was reliable.

Asset universe: MOD, JCI, ETN, TT and CARR
Historical period: Oct 2008-Jul 2026 for JCI and ETN; Nov 2009-Jul 2026 for MOD; Apr-May 2025-Jul 2026 for TT and CARR
Data and features used: Delayed ONI/delta ONI; lagged copper, aluminum and nickel returns; monthly stock returns
Model or trading rule: Separate expanding ONI-to-stock and metal-to-stock rules with frozen 12-month blocks
Important parameters: Same publication-delay and cost rules as VRT; no shared cross-sectional portfolio optimization
Main result: MOD ONI and metal rules lost 8.62% and 11.56% annualized; JCI metal gained 1.05%; ETN metal lost 1.74%; short-history TT and CARR rules were materially negative.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because results were weak or negative, lags were unstable and the newest listings had too little history.

Asset universe: XOM, CVX, COP, EOG, OXY, SLB, MPC, PSX, KMI, WMB and XLE; SPY and XLE benchmarks
Historical period: Ticker and horizon dependent through Jul 2026; 159-272 observations for leading tests
Data and features used: NOAA ONI and delta ONI; 1, 3, 6 and 12-month company returns relative to SPY or XLE
Model or trading rule: Predictive linear regressions with HAC standard errors and global/family Benjamini-Hochberg correction
Important parameters: 168 tests; forward-return overlap handled by HAC; candidate ranking by effect size and q-value, not by high p-value
Main result: Nine tests survived global q<0.05. ONI to COP-XLE at 6 months was strongest: r=-0.478, p=0.000018, q=0.0031, n=164.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as the strongest descriptive cross-asset lead. It was not accepted as a trading strategy because overlapping horizons and common factors remain.

Asset universe: Same US energy universe relative to SPY and XLE
Historical period: Seven eligible historical El Niño peaks through Jul 2026
Data and features used: Peak dates from NOAA ONI; post-peak 1, 3, 6 and 12-month relative returns
Model or trading rule: Average event-window relative return with event-count inference and Benjamini-Hochberg correction
Important parameters: Only seven events at most; later-listed firms had fewer; no row-level monthly replication treated as an independent event
Main result: No peak event-study relationship survived global multiple-testing correction.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the independent event count was too small and mean event results were unstable.

Asset universe: Same energy companies and XLE
Historical period: May 2010-Jul 2026 for long-history names; Apr 2020-Jul 2026 for later test windows
Data and features used: Delayed peak confirmation; monthly company returns; benchmark context
Model or trading rule: Trade each company only after an eligible ONI peak was confirmable; hold for the frozen rule interval
Important parameters: Costs charged; 2-5 out-of-sample peak events depending on ticker; HAC mean test
Main result: PSX cumulative +76.7% and COP +57.3%, each with only two OOS events and p=0.162 or 0.182; SLB -53.5%; XLE -37.1%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because large cumulative returns came from very few events and no strategy mean was significant.

Asset universe: Long XLE and short COP pair
Data and features used: Delayed positive strong-ENSO states; COP/XLE adjusted daily returns; distributions; market-regime features
Model or trading rule: Five frozen signal definitions across 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 and 60-trading-day horizons; direction learned from earlier completed signals
Important parameters: Two-month embargo; 35 rule/horizon combinations; pair weights +0.5 XLE and -0.5 COP; 10 bp per order; simplified 37% tax on positive gains
Main result: Best ex-post rule was strong-but-cooling at 40 days: two trades, 5.30% gross, 4.89% net pre-tax, 3.08% after tax, 100% win rate.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained only as a research template. Two trades from one 2023-2024 episode cannot validate the selected winner from 35 combinations.

Asset universe: XLE call options
Data and features used: Frozen H6 signal; historical option chain; exact entry and exit bars; underlying spot
Model or trading rule: Buy one point-in-time ATM XLE call and sell the same contract at the frozen exit
Important parameters: Nearest strike to spot; expiration at least 7 days after planned exit and closest to 75 DTE; 10% debit budget; 2.5% haircut each option transaction; $0.65 per contract per leg
Main result: After-tax return on initial capital -12.72%; both trades lost money.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because XLE upside did not exceed premium decay and modeled friction.

Asset universe: COP put options
Data and features used: Frozen H6 signal; historical COP option chain; exact entry and exit bars
Model or trading rule: Buy one point-in-time ATM COP put and sell the same contract at the frozen exit
Important parameters: Expiration at least 7 days after planned exit and closest to 75 DTE; 10% debit budget; 2.5% transaction haircut; $0.65 per contract per leg
Main result: Capital deployed $20,116; after-tax profit $8,344; 8.34% return on initial capital; 65.84% return on deployed debit; two winning trades.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as a candidate payoff shape because convex COP downside matched the realized path. It remains unvalidated with only two trades and no historical IV surface.

Experiment name or identifier: EXP-21 Long XLE call plus COP put
Asset universe: XLE call and COP put
Data and features used: Frozen pair signal; point-in-time chains; exact option bars
Model or trading rule: Buy an ATM XLE call and an ATM COP put; close both at the frozen exit
Important parameters: Two long legs; 10% risk budget; expiration rule near 75 DTE; same option haircuts and fees
Main result: After-tax return -0.38%; one of two trades profitable.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because premium on both legs absorbed the modest pair payoff.

Asset universe: Long and short XLE calls
Data and features used: Frozen signal; point-in-time strikes and expirations; exact option bars
Model or trading rule: Buy the lower-strike XLE call and sell a higher-strike call with the same expiration
Important parameters: 10% risk budget; expiration rule near 75 DTE; same option costs on both legs
Main result: After-tax return -11.44%; no winning trades.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the capped-upside structure did not overcome debit and friction.

Asset universe: XLE call spread and COP put spread
Data and features used: Frozen signal; four option legs selected from point-in-time chains
Model or trading rule: Combine an XLE bull call spread with a COP bear put spread and close all legs at the frozen exit
Important parameters: 10% risk budget; same expiration rule; 2.5% haircut on every option transaction plus per-contract fees
Main result: After-tax return +1.66%; both trades profitable; return on deployed debit 13.70%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained only as a secondary structure. It reduced premium exposure but the sample remained two trades.

Asset universe: Data centers in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, North Dakota and Ohio; per-100-MW results for five additional states
Data and features used: ENSO state-temperature estimate; EIA June 2026 commercial electricity rates; LBNL PUE context; Lau-Tsai state data-center capacity
Model or trading rule: Incremental MWh equals facility MW times 744 hours times 70% utilization times incremental PUE; multiply by state USD/MWh rate
Important parameters: Base PUE 1.30; cooling component 0.24; delta-PUE per C of 0.0075 low, 0.015 central and 0.030 high
Main result: Central incremental December electricity cost $9.19m across six capacity-disclosed states; sensitivity $2.19m-$28.59m.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Accepted as a physical operating-cost scenario with explicit sensitivities. It was not treated as equipment capex or supplier revenue.

Asset universe: Same affected-state data-center capacity
Data and features used: NOAA temperatures; state design-temperature context; ASHRAE engineering guidance; JLL procurement lead times; operator cooling disclosures
Model or trading rule: Screen whether forecast winter temperature crosses a design/procurement threshold for new equipment; calculate separate audit contingency sensitivity
Important parameters: About 33-week equipment lead time; forecast window 12-16 weeks; state capacity applied only where separately disclosed
Main result: Central identifiable ENSO-driven new-equipment capex $0. Hypothetical audit screen $5.80m central with $2.34m-$28.13m range.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected as a near-term event-capex trade because winter warming did not create a demonstrated design shortfall and procurement would already need to be underway.

Asset universe: MOD, AAON, VRT, NVT, JCI, TT, SPXC, FIX and EME
Data and features used: Supplier filings and investor releases; ASHRAE/JLL research; Microsoft, Meta and Google site/cooling disclosures; state capacity pipeline
Model or trading rule: Qualitative ranking by data-center cooling exposure, publicly evidenced orders/backlog and relevance to affected states
Important parameters: No unverified site-level vendor award accepted; event revenue kept separate from secular pipeline revenue
Main result: Secular cooling demand was well evidenced, but no credible incremental 2026 ENSO revenue allocation could be assigned by supplier.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as a supplier universe for the secular theme. Modified to remove claims that ENSO itself caused disclosed orders or backlog.

Asset universe: MOD, AAON, VRT, NVT, JCI, TT, SPXC and equal-weight basket; XLI factor
Historical period: Ticker histories from Feb 2004 or later through Aug 2026; VRT from Mar 2020; forecast Oct-Dec 2026
Data and features used: Monthly XLI, copper, aluminum, nickel, ONI, delta ONI, Midwest temperature and stock returns
Model or trading rule: Ticker ridge factor models plus three-month residual block bootstrap across 27 ONI by temperature by metals cells
Important parameters: 10,000 paths per cell; historical intercept set to zero; alpha selected by blocked validation; preserve cross-company residual dependence
Main result: Central basket median +4.62%, P5 -20.67%, P95 +26.34%. Median across all cells about +2.8% to +7.0%. NVT OOS R-squared -0.498.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as a sensitivity and risk-fan tool. Rejected as a precise forecast because climate-cell differences were small beside market and residual uncertainty.

Asset universe: MOD, AAON, VRT, NVT, JCI, TT and SPXC
Data and features used: Issuer news metadata and text; counts of ENSO, AI, cooling, orders, backlog and capacity terms; event-window stock returns
Model or trading rule: Compare climate-specific news attention with broader cooling/AI attention and inspect stock returns around ENSO news dates
Important parameters: Prior-month availability convention; no absence-of-keyword result treated as direct proof of pricing
Main result: Zero explicit ENSO mentions for all seven names; cooling/AI terms dominated; stock reactions around ENSO news dates were mixed.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as evidence that ENSO was not a major explicit narrative. Modified because keyword absence cannot show that weather expectations were absent from price.

Asset universe: MOD, AAON, VRT, NVT, JCI, TT and SPXC; XLI benchmark and hedge
Data and features used: Three-month-delayed rolling AR(1) ONI surprise; capacity-weighted cooling-degree proxy; lagged fundamental news; relative momentum; cooling-exposure purity; XLI regime
Model or trading rule: Hold at most two confirmed stocks; six-month inverse-vol weights; 100% or 50% gross by XLI regime; partial or full beta hedge
Important parameters: ONI above +0.5 and rising or surprising; signal rank 35% news, 45% relative momentum, 20% purity; 15 bp per unit turnover
Main result: Total return 25.48%; CAGR 4.42%; vol 7.53%; Sharpe 0.61; max drawdown -3.38%; HAC p=0.308; 8 active months.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained only as a small risk satellite. Low drawdown came partly from cash and hedging, while the active sample and statistical evidence were weak.

Asset universe: Equal cooling-stock basket
Data and features used: Three-month-delayed ONI level and cooling-stock returns
Model or trading rule: Long the cooling basket whenever the delayed ONI rule is active
Important parameters: No news confirmation, cooling proxy, cross-sectional ranking or beta hedge; 15 bp turnover convention
Main result: Total return 58.68%; CAGR 9.19%; Sharpe 0.74; max drawdown -9.99%; HAC p=0.246.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected as the primary rule because it had no significant mean evidence, depended on one strong episode and did not isolate climate alpha from the thematic rally.

Asset universe: Equal-weight MOD, AAON, VRT, NVT, JCI, TT and SPXC
Data and features used: Adjusted monthly stock returns
Model or trading rule: Always-invested equal-weight basket with monthly rebalancing and cost convention
Important parameters: 100% gross; no climate timing; same current-name universe
Main result: Total return 384.26%; CAGR 35.05%; Sharpe 1.11; max drawdown -30.83%; HAC p=0.0147.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Kept as the thematic benchmark. It cannot be interpreted as ENSO alpha because AI/data-center growth, market beta and survivor selection dominate.

Asset universe: Confirmed cooling-stock strategy
Data and features used: Resampled market, metal and cross-company residual blocks; current ONI, cooling, news and relative-momentum states
Model or trading rule: 20,000 conditional paths for Excellent, Normal and Conservative cases
Important parameters: Excellent adds explicit positive cooling repricing; Normal adds no extra uplift; Conservative keeps climate sleeve in cash
Main result: Median returns: Excellent +17.14% with P10 -7.48% and P90 +40.98%; Normal +4.61% with P10 -9.42% and P90 +16.80%; Conservative 0%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained for scenario sizing only. The cases are definitions rather than calibrated probabilities and six of seven latest forecast models had negative blocked OOS R-squared.

Asset universe: VRT, MOD, ETN, PWR and GEV options
Data and features used: Historical option chains; exact call and put bars; underlying prices; FX; NOAA ONI as context
Model or trading rule: Buy same-strike ATM call and put monthly; close on planned exit; capital-constrained sizing
Important parameters: HKD 100,000 per ticker path; no leverage; 2.5% haircut per option transaction; $0.65 per contract per leg side
Main result: Returns through 11 Sep: VRT -28.59%, MOD -29.39%, ETN -63.04%, PWR -42.08%, GEV -3.04%. One-contract shadow PnL was negative for every ticker.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because realized volatility did not exceed the combined option premium and friction. Thin volume and large debit worsened execution quality.

Asset universe: VRT, MOD, ETN, PWR and GEV options
Data and features used: Same exact option data plus delayed positive ONI gate
Model or trading rule: Run the monthly straddle only when the delayed ONI rule is active
Important parameters: Same capital and cost assumptions; completed-only results reported separately
Main result: Completed gated VRT +8.06% from 2 trades and MOD +1.57% from 1 trade; ETN -35.83%; PWR -43.38%; GEV had no completed executable trade.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because apparent winners had one or two trades, while most names lost heavily and liquidity coverage was poor.

Experiment name or identifier: EXP-35 Insurer ONI company correlation screen
Asset universe: 60 supplied insurers; 58 with usable bars; KIE and SPY benchmarks
Historical period: Ticker dependent from Sep 2003 or listing date through 11 Sep 2026
Data and features used: Three-month-delayed revised ONI; monthly insurer returns; delta ONI; market-relative returns; severe-event flags
Model or trading rule: Company Pearson and HAC regressions plus Benjamini-Hochberg correction
Important parameters: Severe ONI at least +1.5 C; current 2026-active universe; split-adjusted prices excluding dividends
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Retained as a descriptive anomaly only. Each young company had one completed severe episode plus partial 2026 data and substantial survivor bias.

Experiment name or identifier: EXP-36 Severe-El-Niño insurer basket event test
Asset universe: Equal-weight catastrophe/property insurer basket; KIE and SPY
Data and features used: Delayed ONI severe-state flag; insurer, KIE and SPY monthly returns
Model or trading rule: Compare mean severe-month return with other months using HAC and market-relative controls
Important parameters: Severe threshold +1.5 C; no same-month revised ONI use
Main result: Insurer basket mean +1.45% in severe months versus +0.60% otherwise; difference +0.85 percentage points; HAC p=0.503.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because there was no statistically reliable common selloff or rally across insurers.

Asset universe: ROOT, PLMR, KNSL, MCY, LMND, CINF, PGR, AIZ, AIG, BAP, ALL and HIG
Historical period: Eligible severe-ENSO windows in 2015-2016, 2023-2024 and 2026 through 11 Sep; ticker coverage varies
Data and features used: Delayed ONI; SMA20 and SMA60; five-day momentum; ATR10; weekly NBBO imbalance; short interest; short volume; shares outstanding
Model or trading rule: Daily composite long/short score; next-session-open execution; ATR trailing stop; forced event-window close
Important parameters: ONI delay 3 months; 2.5 times ATR stop; 7.5 bp per side; 3% annual short borrow; 20% tax on positive realized event gains; 100% max gross
Main result: Linked-period return -21.92%; Sharpe -0.45; max drawdown -26.32%; active hit rate 48.4%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the composite overtraded without directional edge and short/quote data were unavailable for much of the historical sample.

Experiment name or identifier: EXP-38 Core insurer moving-average and ATR strategy
Asset universe: Same 12 insurers
Historical period: Same eligible peak windows through 11 Sep 2026
Data and features used: Delayed ONI; SMA20, SMA60, five-day momentum and ATR10; no dependence on sparse short/order-book features
Model or trading rule: Daily price-trend score with next-open execution and ATR trailing stop
Important parameters: 2.5 times ATR stop; 7.5 bp per side; 20% positive-gain tax; 100% max gross
Main result: Linked-period return -24.75%; Sharpe -0.31; max drawdown -30.12%; active hit rate 48.6%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the simplified price-only features also lacked directional edge and ATR exits often crystallized short-lived price noise.

Asset universe: MOD, AAON, VRT, NVT, JCI, TT and SPXC
Data and features used: Monthly adjusted returns; XLI benchmark
Model or trading rule: Monthly equal-weight, fully invested long basket
Important parameters: 15 bp one-way turnover cost; no leverage; zero cash yield; no tax
Main result: CAGR 35.01%; vol 31.93%; Sharpe 1.11; max drawdown -30.83%; ending HKD 483,531 from HKD 100,000.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Kept as the return and drawdown comparator. Rejected as the preferred risk policy because drawdown exceeded 30% and the universe benefited from a strong thematic rally.

Asset universe: Same seven cooling stocks
Data and features used: Prior 12 monthly stock returns
Model or trading rule: Weights proportional to inverse trailing volatility with water-filling redistribution above the name cap
Important parameters: 25% maximum name weight; 100% gross; no leverage; 15 bp turnover cost
Main result: CAGR 31.80%; vol 29.39%; max drawdown -29.51%; retained 90.8% of basic CAGR but reduced drawdown only 4.3%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected as the final policy because it did not materially improve drawdown despite retaining return.

Asset universe: Same seven cooling stocks
Data and features used: Capped inverse-vol weights and prior 12-month shadow-core volatility
Model or trading rule: Scale gross by minimum of 1 and 20% divided by trailing annualized volatility
Important parameters: 20% target; no leverage; 15 bp turnover cost
Main result: CAGR 21.69%; vol 22.65%; max drawdown -26.57%; CAGR retention 62.0%; drawdown reduction 13.8%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because it retained enough CAGR but did not meet the 30% drawdown-reduction gate.

Asset universe: Same seven cooling stocks; XLI regime indicator
Data and features used: Capped inverse-vol core; prior XLI close; six-month XLI mean; three-month XLI return
Model or trading rule: Use 100% gross when prior XLI is above its six-month mean and three-month return is positive; otherwise 50%
Important parameters: No leverage; 15 bp turnover cost; all regime inputs lagged
Main result: CAGR 23.69%; vol 23.33%; max drawdown -23.48%; CAGR retention 67.7%; drawdown reduction 23.8%.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Rejected because the loss reduction did not reach the predeclared 30% gate.

Asset universe: Same seven cooling stocks
Data and features used: Capped inverse-vol core and prior fully observed shadow-portfolio wealth
Model or trading rule: Scale gross according to prior shadow drawdown; use shadow series for recovery even while the live policy is de-risked
Important parameters: 100% gross above -10% drawdown; 50% from -10% to -20%; 25% below -20%; no leverage; 15 bp turnover cost
Main result: CAGR 27.13%; vol 24.12%; max drawdown -20.59%; CAGR retention 77.5%; drawdown reduction 33.2%; ending HKD 352,600.
Why it was accepted, modified or rejecte: Accepted as the only policy meeting the predeclared gate of at least 50% CAGR retention, at least 30% drawdown reduction and no leverage. It still requires future validation.

Asset universe: Same seven cooling stocks
